description: Single-panel horizontal bar chart (no sub-panels) plotting "Mean grain size (µm)" on the x-axis, ruled from 0 to 100 with major ticks every 20 µm and minor ticks at 10 µm intervals. The y-axis carries four unlabelled tick positions; each alloy is identified by a text label printed beside its bar. All four bars are filled light blue with black outlines, ordered top to bottom: 9.7Al-0.04C-0.09Ti, 8.1Al-0.0015C-0.14Ti, 6.8Al-0.0035C-0.10Ti, and IF (traditional Al-free interstitial-free ferritic steel). The longest bar is 8.1Al-0.0015C-0.14Ti, ending beyond the 80 µm gridline, between the 80 and 100 µm ticks and close to 90 µm. 6.8Al-0.0035C-0.10Ti is second, ending just below the 70 µm mark between the 60 and 80 µm gridlines. The 9.7Al-0.04C-0.09Ti and IF bars are the two shortest and nearly equal, both terminating just short of the 20 µm gridline. No numeric data labels, error bars, legend or scale bar appear on the panel. The figure demonstrates that ultralow-C Fe-Al low-density steels containing sufficient stabilizer (6.8 and 8.1 wt.% Al) attain much coarser grains than traditional IF steel, whereas the higher-C, under-stabilized 9.7 wt.% Al steel retains an IF-like fine grain size.

observations.observation: The figure is a horizontal bar chart whose x-axis is labelled "Mean grain size (µm)", ruled 0-100 with major ticks at 0, 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100 and minor ticks at 10 µm intervals.
Four bars are plotted, labelled top to bottom exactly as "9.7Al-0.04C-0.09Ti", "8.1Al-0.0015C-0.14Ti", "6.8Al-0.0035C-0.10Ti" and "IF"; the y-axis itself has no numeric scale or title.
The 8.1Al-0.0015C-0.14Ti bar is the longest, extending past the 80 µm gridline and ending between the 80 and 100 µm ticks, close to 90 µm; no value is printed on the bar.
The 6.8Al-0.0035C-0.10Ti bar is the second longest, ending between the 60 and 80 µm gridlines just below the midpoint, i.e. slightly under 70 µm.
The 9.7Al-0.04C-0.09Ti bar and the IF bar are the two shortest and are nearly equal in length, both ending just short of the 20 µm gridline.
No numeric data labels, error bars, legend, inset or scale bar are present on the panel; values can only be inferred from the gridlines.
The caption states the bars compare the typical grain size of Fe-Al ferritic low-density steels with an Al-free (traditional IF) ferritic steel.

The caption states that low-density steels with ultralow C and sufficient "stabilizer" (the 6.8 and 8.1 wt.% Al steels) have larger grain sizes than traditional IF steel, whereas the steel with higher C and insufficient stabilizing element (9.7 wt.% Al steel) has a fine grain size compared with IF steel.
The citing text states that Al added in small amounts (<0.04 wt.%) as a deoxidizer causes grain refinement probably through Zener drag exerted by AlN particles.
The citing text states that low-density ferritic steels containing high amounts of solute Al exhibit coarser grains than low carbon steels, though the results were mixed up with processing effects.
The citing text states that the presence of free C in the matrix refines the grain size, possibly by the solute drag effect of C.

The alloy labels show the 9.7 wt.% Al steel carries the highest C level in the set (0.04C) and the lowest Ti (0.09Ti), consistent with the caption's description of it as having higher C and insufficient stabilizing element.
